# Input otp

Separate boxes for a one-time code.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill odv-pill-out">Left out of Content first</span> Forms are rare and short: newsletter and search. Actions are rare: subscribe, share, save. No step asks for a one-time code. <span class="odv-instead">Use instead: <a href="./input">Input</a></span></p>

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** A short code sent by text or email, typed or pasted.
- **Not when:** Passwords or any value that is not a fixed-length code.

Instead:

- [Input](./input.md): Any other short value.

## Words

- Write to one person: "you", not "users".
- Short sentences with room to breathe.
- Explain why before asking for anything.
- Use: Read, Save for later, You, Next issue. Avoid: Click here, Submit, Users, Content.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Not now
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Browse guides

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] Screen readers hear one field with a label, and pasting the whole code works. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add input-otp
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Variables

Every token Input otp reads, from its code: the variable, the semantic token it aliases, and where that ends in the theme.

### Read straight from the system

Input otp has no variables of its own yet; it reads these system tokens directly.
